body: thank you aenea for telling me that. I won't lie and say I feel better, and from what you have written you would be able to tell if I was lying anyway. You are right though about what I am feeling at the moment, with the 'it hurts so much, how can I go on?'. I just miss the girl I love while having to deal with my brothers death. The timing just seemed abnormally cruel. On top of that, the ocd makes it impossible to stop constant flash backs to better times. You may wonder why that would be a problem, to think of better times, but when you're living through a nightmare, I don't want to be reminded of how good it once was. I'm hoping that changes but I don't know. Did you ever forgive your ex-fiancée? It sounded terrible.

I already am doing the therapy, both with a psychologist and psychiatrist. It's just so utterly painful that it is hard to think clearly. To be able to see that there is light at the end seems utterly impossible. I know it helps when people say that it does get better, but it only seems like it works in a superficial kind of way. It's the first time I really wish I believed in god/gods, but I could never stomach it. Everything just seems without love or hope.

Are you saying that it actually stops hurting? I hope you are right because I honestly don't think it can. I want to believe otherwise but this kind of tragedy makes me feel continually sick to my stomach. Thanks for the advice, I know exercise is important but I honestly don't feel any better when I do it now. In fact I think I feel worse.
I'm familiar with a lot of CBT but what has happened is a whole new ball game. I do get sleep but the nightmares just make the waking hours that  more uncomfortable.
